what_its_for: Maribavir is an antiviral medicine used to treat a viral infection called cytomegalovirus (CMV) in adults and children (12 years and older, weighing at least 35 kg) who have had an organ or stem cell transplant. It is used when other antiviral medicines did not work or caused too many side effects.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets. Take this medicine at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. If you have trouble swallowing tablets, talk to your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and qualifying children is 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) taken by mouth TWICE daily (every 12 hours). Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 6 hours away. If your next dose is less than 6 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store maribavir tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking maribavir with ganciclovir or valganciclovir (other antiviral medicines for CMV), because maribavir may make those medicines work less well. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with maribavir. Avoid starting new medications without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical help if you experience: changes in your taste (a very common side effect — let your doctor know if it is bothersome); nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that is severe or does not go away; tiredness or fatigue that is unusual; signs of low blood sugar if you have diabetes (dizziness, shakiness, sweating); any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Maribavir starts working against the CMV virus right away, but you may not feel better immediately. Treatment typically lasts about 8 weeks, but your doctor will monitor you with blood tests to check if the virus levels in your blood are going down. It is very important to take ALL doses as prescribed, even if you feel better, to make sure the infection is fully treated.
special_populations: Children: Maribavir can be used in children 12 years and older who weigh at least 35 kg (about 77 lbs). The dose is the same as adults. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of maribavir during pregnancy is not fully known. It is not known if maribavir passes into breast milk, so discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or Liver Problems: Dose adjustments are generally not needed for mild to moderate kidney or liver problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney or liver issues so they can monitor you closely. Older Adults: No specific dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you carefully.
